newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court hears rights group closure case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court hears rights group closure case.

text.p: A Turkish criminal court on Tuesday began to try human rights activists on a legal technicality in a case that could lead to the closure of the country's main human rights group.
The court heard a petition from a prosecutor to outlaw the Human Rights Association because its founding charter is allegedly anti-constitutional.

"The court prosecutor claims our charter, which says an application for membership can be rejected without giving any reason, breaks the constitution and law of associations," lawyer and group member Selahattin Esmer told Reuters.
The Human Rights Association, established in 1986, has long drawn official anger because of its accusations of widespread human rights abuses that Ankara says damage the country's image abroad.
The European Parliament is holding back hundreds of millions of dollars of financial aid to Turkey, saying the country's rights record must be improved.
Association chairman Akin Birdal told reporters there was no justification for the trial because the group had changed the article in its charter that the prosecutor objected to.
The association would be outlawed if Birdal and other leading members were found guilty of misconduct in drawing up the charter but the activists would face no personal punishment.
